title: Bull in China
premise: The china shop's most fragile piece is a tiny porcelain elephant. The bull is the one tiptoeing. He is sweating through a bow tie.
visual: Aisle of teacups and plates. A huge nervous bull in a tiny bow tie, on tiptoe, two fingers of hoof holding a teacup. Pedestal in the center: a palm-sized porcelain elephant with a price tag that is just a dollar sign. Sweat drops. A mouse shopkeeper watching with a feather duster, equally nervous.
characterLean: Idiom with the polarity flipped. Cutaway after anyone says they will be careful. The mouse is management. The bull is trying.
grokImaginePrompt: 2D hand-drawn cel animation frame in early-1990s Warner Bros. television cartoon style, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, 4:3: a china shop aisle packed with teacups and plates, a huge nervous cartoon bull in a tiny bow tie standing on tiptoe holding a teacup with two hoof-fingers, giant sweat drops flying off the bull, on a central pedestal a palm-sized porcelain elephant figurine with a tiny price tag that is only a dollar sign, a mouse shopkeeper on a ladder watching with a feather duster equally nervous, shelves receding, thick confident black ink outlines with slight taper, flat saturated cel color fills with one hard-edged shadow tone and no gradients on the characters, painted gouache shop interior, faint cel dust, hand-drawn cartoon, Grok Imagine style
motion: 6-second lockoff. The bull's knee wobbles. The teacup rattles. The porcelain elephant does not move. One sweat drop hits a saucer and rings. The mouse covers its eyes. Nothing breaks. Hold the tiptoe.
notes: Tiny elephant vs huge bull is the still — if they are the same scale the reverse-idiom dies. No shop-name lettering. Do not smash the aisle on the last frame; the joke is the care, not the crash. Distinct from mailbox-mallard slapstick: this one is not allowed to connect.
